translationRepairs: Dou Ying, courtesy name Wangsun, was the son of a cousin of Empress Xiaowen.
Dou Ying, courtesy name Wangsun, was the son of a paternal cousin of Empress Xiaowen.
Chinese 從兄子 specifically means son of a paternal male cousin; 'a cousin' is underspecified.
He appointed Dou Ying grand marshal and gave him a thousand catties of gold.
He appointed Dou Ying general-in-chief (da jiangjun) and gave him a thousand catties of gold.
大將軍 is general-in-chief/grand general, not 'grand marshal' (太尉).
At every weighty court debate, Marquis Zhou Yafu and Marquis Dou Ying were preeminent—no other marquis dared claim equal precedence with them.
At every weighty court debate, the Marquis of Tiao and the Marquis of Weiqi stood so high that none of the other marquises dared match them in ceremony.
Chinese names them by titles 條侯、魏其; the idiomatic gloss invents 'Zhou Yafu' and 'Dou Ying' not present in this unit's Chinese.
He was summoned to court as grand marshal of the imperial stud.
He was summoned to court as minister of the imperial coach-houses (taipu).
太僕 is the minister of the imperial stud/coach-houses, not 'grand marshal'.
Next he reached Marquis Guan Xian of Linying, who was whispering to Cheng Bushi and never rose from his mat.
Next he reached Marquis Guan Xian of Linru, who was whispering to Cheng Bushi and never rose from his mat.
Chinese 臨汝侯 is Marquis of Linru; the idiomatic text has Linying.
